observations.evidence: Single hooked upright with a low curved foot; there are no distinct i and d strokes. The 2-like/wriggle alternatives remain.
After the tall split(t) strokes a detached short flat ending precedes a separate comma. It does not securely distinguish compressed e from an abbreviation stop; no acute or second e is visible.
The canceled low group after d apostrophe is heavily joined and crossed; probable une remains uncertain. The tall loop and following apostrophe of live l ext. are distinct.
A separate short low terminal is visible after the main cursive noun. It favors the final r but does not securely rule out a compressed extra s.
The contracted low joining strokes do not isolate a secure o or terminal letter.
There is a heavy horizontal middle/end over a low loop, but it cannot be cleanly separated into a cancellation stroke and the word joins. Both lexical and state doubts remain.
A diagonal old Z-like underform is visible beneath the double upright F; the superimposed strokes obscure whether the old diagonal was doubled.
A long horizontal cancellation leaves only an initial high hook and low protrusion. No whole word can be read; it follows the second encore and comma.
Broad outer sweep with inner curl and raised right tip; decorative alphabet remains uncertain.
The index begins with a small high hook, descends to a low bend, and exits in a rightward rising foot; it has no n-like arch with a terminal downstroke.
The smooth open bowl and short internal right stem support calligraphic/plain cursive A, not a secure Fraktur shape.
The lower-left relation is heavily retraced and its strokes nearly cross. A curved left component favors simeq, but the original two-stroke shape is not secure enough to remove equality.
Two oblique old strokes and their top/base remain distinguishable behind the live double upright F.
The upper relation below Aff has a clearly wavy left component and separate straight right bar; a single wr omits one component.
The upper Z-to-G shaft ends in a small tapered spur without two independently visible wings. Headless shaft and abbreviated arrow remain possible.
The lower first shaft has a downturned terminal with no definite upper wing; its head status remains uncertain.
